stack-order.why: push adds to the top and pop removes from the top: last in, first out. peek looks at the new top without removing it.

queue-order.why: A queue is first in, first out: poll removes the oldest element, "a", leaving b and c in order.

brackets.why: The most recently opened bracket must close first: that's last in, first out. A counter can't tell "([)]" (unbalanced) from "([])", and a queue checks in the wrong order.

why-arraydeque.why: Stack pays for synchronization nobody needs here and inherits Vector's index-based methods. ArrayDeque is the documented replacement. (It does not accept null elements.)

bracket-steps.why: Create the stack, scan the characters (pushing openers, matching closers), then make sure nothing was left open.

monotonic-stack.why: Every index is pushed once and popped at most once, so the inner loop runs at most n times in total across the whole scan.

queue-removes.why: That's a stack. A queue removes the oldest element first (first in, first out).
